### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **11** package(s): `@objectstack/cli`, `@objectstack/client`, `@objectstack/core`, `@objectstack/lint`, `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/platform-objects`, `packages/plugins`, `@objectstack/rest`, `@objectstack/runtime`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **210** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **19** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/cli/package.json`, `packages/core/src/fallbacks/index.ts`, `packages/lint/src/validate-sortable-fields.ts`, …), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**102** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json f09d4122bc8c2eb39414b83b1924217a04b66cb2`.

⛔ **11** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **19** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/cli/package.json`, `packages/core/src/fallbacks/index.ts`, `packages/lint/src/validate-sortable-fields.ts`, …) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **2** cross-cutting symbol(s) contributed no route anchor: `tenantId (7 routes)`, `isSystem (5 routes)`
- **4** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `created_at (symbol, 34 pages)`, `owner_id (symbol, 31 pages)`, `owner_id (literal, 31 pages)`, `sys_user (literal, 37 pages)`
- **37** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **207** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **153** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **153**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **98** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **154** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json f09d4122bc8c2eb39414b83b1924217a04b66cb2` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `4adae22f9950458e57fe0aebfd63fdceb5847261` — the merge of head `e4ead748dfe6e589a00cde829769643a6b51d0af` into base `f09d4122bc8c2eb39414b83b1924217a04b66cb2`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 4adae22f9950458e57fe0aebfd63fdceb5847261 && git checkout 4adae22f9950458e57fe0aebfd63fdceb5847261
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin f09d4122bc8c2eb39414b83b1924217a04b66cb2 e4ead748dfe6e589a00cde829769643a6b51d0af && git checkout -B drift-repro f09d4122bc8c2eb39414b83b1924217a04b66cb2 && git merge --no-ff e4ead748dfe6e589a00cde829769643a6b51d0af

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json f09d4122bc8c2eb39414b83b1924217a04b66cb2
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs f09d4122bc8c2eb39414b83b1924217a04b66cb2` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `aab0e0fc60c55128f0d0640b690712b3d85a3b05`

CI at the head: 44 check-runs, all `success` or `skipped`, none failed (Lint & Repo Gates, Type Check x4, Test Core 6/6, Dogfood 3/3, Check Changeset, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Spec property liveness all green).

### ① Derived judgments

1. **`report` metadata kind untouched — RIGHT.** The diff touches no file under `packages/spec/src/ui/report*`, no analytics or dataset schema; `packages/spec/src/stack.zod.ts:381` (`reports: z.array(ReportSchema)`) and the nav rule at `stack.zod.ts:2688-2738` are unchanged. The only `stack.zod.ts` hunk is `validateKnownCapabilities` (3257-3282). `content/docs/ui/apps.mdx` now points the nav item at `report` metadata by `reportName`, which is the live surface.

2. **`defineStack` door — RIGHT.** `packages/spec/src/stack.zod.ts:3275-3278` refuses `reports` with `RETIRED_PLATFORM_CAPABILITY_GUIDANCE.reports` under the registered `STACK_CAPABILITY_UNKNOWN` (422), deduped, and a misspelling (`reportz`) still gets the typo text. Pinned with an ablation-sensitive test at `packages/spec/src/kernel/reports-capability-retirement.test.ts:74-109` (envelope, prescription content, control token, distinct messages).

3. **`os serve` door (older artifact) — RIGHT, with a note.** `packages/cli/src/commands/serve.ts:4614-4624` prints the retirement prescription (not the typo text) and continues. It is a warn-and-ignore, not a refusal, but that is serve's documented pre-existing posture for every unknown declared token ("Warn-first: intended to become a hard error", serve.ts:4600-4603), and it is loud with the correct prescription. Acceptable.

4. **`os validate` / `os build` door — WRONG (under-reach on the card's "every door" acceptance).** Both commands accept a plain-object config (`packages/cli/src/utils/config.ts:410` `mod.default || mod`; e2e fixtures use `export default {` — `packages/cli/test/build-json-advisory-parity.e2e.test.ts:133-135`), parse it with `ObjectStackDefinitionSchema.safeParse` (`compile.ts:347`, `validate.ts:283`), whose `requires` is `z.array(z.string())` with no vocabulary check (`stack.zod.ts:799`), and then run `preflightRequiredCapabilities` (`compile.ts:611`, `validate.ts:515`). For `reports`, `classifyRequiredCapability` returns `unknown` (`platform-capabilities.ts:422`) and `renderCapabilityMessage` prints exactly the misleading text: `requires: "reports" is not a known platform capability — check for a typo.` (`packages/cli/src/utils/capability-preflight.ts:96`) — as a non-fatal advisory. So at this door the token is neither refused nor prescribed; the card's acceptance ("refused at parse or validate with a message naming the retirement and the replacement") is not met, and the PR's own claim that "the refusal and the serve warning share one text" leaves out the third reader of the same vocabulary. Only when the config file itself calls `defineStack` does the import throw first.

5. **Enumerations — token removed from enum, provider map, CLI map, docs, generated JSON — MOSTLY RIGHT, one miss.** Removed from `PLATFORM_CAPABILITY_TOKENS` (`platform-capabilities.ts:63`), `PLATFORM_CAPABILITY_PROVIDERS` (:211), serve `CAPABILITY_PROVIDERS` and `NEEDS_JOB_OR_QUEUE` (`serve.ts:2004`, `:2822`), `PLATFORM_OBJECTS_BY_PACKAGE`, `api-surface/` + `export-origins/` (regenerated), `llms.txt`, `content/docs/plugins/packages.mdx`, `api/client-sdk.mdx`, `README.md`, `capabilities/*.mdx`; `spec-changes.json` / `docs/protocol-upgrade-guide.md` fold only through the current protocol major 17 (`build-spec-changes.ts:8-9`, `PROTOCOL_VERSION = '17.0.0'`), so no step-18 entry is projected there and `check:spec-changes` is legitimately green. **Missed:** the customer-published skill `skills/objectstack-platform/SKILL.md:369` still lists `` `audit` `email` `sharing` `reports` `approvals` `webhooks` `` → `@objectstack/plugin-` + the token, in the table introduced at :361-363 as the CLI's `CAPABILITY_PROVIDERS` "all 20 of its entries". That table is what a model reads to write `requires`, i.e. exactly the author the new prescription is written for. It is not in the PR body's remaining-hits list. (`skills/**` is Tier H per AGENTS.md:273; the PR is already Tier H.)

6. **`RETIRED_PLATFORM_CAPABILITY_GUIDANCE` disjoint from live tokens — RIGHT, citation wrong.** Frozen, and disjointness is pinned at `reports-capability-retirement.test.ts:60-68`. The docblock at `platform-capabilities.ts:85` says the pin is in `platform-capabilities.test.ts`; that file's :101 test is about `PLATFORM_PLUGIN_WIRED_RUNTIMES`, not this map. Non-blocking doc-accuracy nit.

7. **`/api/v1/reports` answers the standard unmatched-route 404 and is pinned — RIGHT.** `registerReportsEndpoints` deleted (`rest-server.ts:12654` hunk, 340 lines); ledger rows removed (`rest-route-ledger.ts:431`). `packages/rest/src/reports-routes-retired.test.ts` drives the real `HonoHttpServer` with `installNotFoundSeam()`, asserts 404 byte-identical to a never-mounted control, `Allow` absent (not 405), an anti-vacuity route-table check, and a mounted sibling (`/approvals`) answering 401.

8. **RestServer constructor index-10 placeholder — RIGHT.** `rest-server.ts:1683-1692` types the slot `_retiredReportsServiceProvider?: undefined` with a JSDoc naming the #15256 positional hazard; `RestServer` is a public export (`packages/rest/src/index.ts:4`); the only non-test in-repo constructor site is `createRestApiPlugin().start()` (`rest-api-plugin.ts:516`, and `rest-server.zod.ts:32` documents that). A TS caller passing a provider gets TS2345 (it found four stale test callers); a JS caller keeps its later positional bindings intact and the ignored value is harmless. Deleting the slot would silently re-bind arguments 11-20 for JS embedders — worse. Pinned at `rest-api-plugin-slot-lookups.test.ts:142-146, :285-296`, and stated in the changeset.

9. **Other exported-shape changes — judged.** Removed contract exports (8 types, `contracts/index.ts:55`), `client.reports` (`client/src/index.ts:6352`, pinned both at type level via `@ts-expect-error` under `tsconfig.test.json` and at runtime, `client.test.ts:393-407`), 9 `ERROR_CODE_LEDGER` rows (`error-code-ledger.zod.ts:278-280, :290`) under the ledger's retire-with-only-emitter rule — all inside the ruling. New export `RETIRED_PLATFORM_CAPABILITY_GUIDANCE` is necessary and minimal. `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` `INVALID_SORT` hint text re-sourced (patch) — text only, code/status unchanged: acceptable. No over-reach found.

10. **Remaining live references (acceptance grep at head) — three unlisted hits, non-blocking.** Beyond the PR body's seven categories: `packages/runtime/src/external-validation-plugin.ts:240` and `external-validation-shutdown-clears-timers.test.ts:19` still say this plugin "is one of only two `Plugin` implementations in the tree that own `setInterval` (`ReportsServicePlugin` is the other)" — now false in the present tense; `packages/platform-objects/src/apps/translations/object-field-editor-panel-echo-decisions.test.ts:304` cites `sys_saved_report.format` / `sys_report_schedule.format` as current authoring paths (a rationale string only checked for length, :453-455). `.claude/**` roster lines are listed as Tier S follow-ups; ADRs 0021/0029/0053/0073 are history. objectui has no hit; cloud's two test-only readers are confirmed at `capability-coverage.test.ts:45` and `capability-loader.test.ts:475-497`.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/20102-retire-saved-report-stack.md`: `minor` for `@objectstack/spec`, `platform-objects`, `rest`, `client`, `cli`; `patch` for `metadata-protocol`. `minor` for a BREAKING narrowing is the repo's rule (retirement skill `SKILL.md:291-296`; `scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs` rejects `major` in the launch window), the body carries the `**BREAKING**` banner, a FROM → TO line with a one-line fix for each of the seven surfaces, the existing-database statement, `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)`, and exactly one ADR-0087 marker (`adr-0087: registered saved-report-stack-retired`); `Check Changeset` and `check:adr-0087-registration` are green. Packages with comment-only edits (core, lint, objectql, driver-memory) correctly carry no bump; the deleted package cannot. The "removed in @objectstack/spec 17.5.0" wording matches spec at 17.4.0 + minor and the in-flight precedent at `view.zod.ts:2291`.

D3 entry `packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.saved-report-stack-retired.ts`: `id`, `surface` (explicitly excluding the `report` kind), `replacement`, non-empty `reason` (verbatim ruling) and `acceptanceCriteria` (refusal, `classifyRequiredCapability` = unknown, 404, TS2305, tables left in place). Registered under `step18` (`toMajor: 18`, `registry.ts:11877+`) by `gen:migration-registry`, consistent with the other in-flight `18.*` entries. Complete.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Split the ADR-0096 edit?** No — keep it (dev's option A is right). Deleting `report-service.ts` is what turns `check-adr-symbol-anchors` (Lint step 104) red, so the one-line unlink cannot land separately without leaving either PR red; the PR is already a human merge (11.5k lines, AGENTS.md §7 class c) and one Tier H path already makes it Tier H (AGENTS.md:272-273). Note the PR body's governed-path statement now exists (item 3 of its remaining-hits section).
- **Tier H edit at `docs/adr/0096:194`** — truthful and minimal: it removes only the `#isSystem` symbol anchor, keeps the path, `dispatchDue`, the verdict and #2980, and appends "historical and deliberately unlinked: … retired whole by #20102", the phrasing used by ADR-0002/0003/0004 path notes. History preserved, not rewritten. No `anchor-exempt` marker.
- **Physical-tables statement** — the cited convention is real: `packages/cli/src/utils/unmanaged-tables.ts:12-21` ("strands its table forever", "never drops anything, and never proposes a drop", "stays with a human"), `content/docs/deployment/cli.mdx:869`, and the precedent `18.scim-provider-object-retired.ts:49-50`. The D3 entry and changeset state the same.
- **`docs/NORTH-STAR.md:62`** — real: "reports · 报表自己建、自己存、只归自己,还能按时自己发出去 · dashboards · dataset-report-authoring, saved-report-ownership, report-schedule-dispatch-delivery". Two of its three ids are now `status: "retired"`. Tier H, maintainer's edit; the dev's recommendation A (drop the two ids and the scheduled-send leg) matches the ruling that scheduled delivery is out of scope. Not blocking this PR; escalate to the maintainer as a follow-up.
- **Cloud follow-ups** — confirmed at `packages/objectos-runtime/src/capability-coverage.test.ts:45` and `capability-loader.test.ts:475-497` (asserts `pkg: '@objectstack/plugin-reports'`). Both go red on the next spec install; PM-filed per the card.
- **Additional Tier H item surfaced by this review** — `skills/objectstack-platform/SKILL.md:369` (finding ①5). Either the PR fixes the row (it is already Tier H) or the PR body lists it as a remaining hit with a filed follow-up; silently leaving it contradicts the card.

Implemented-by: `claude/issue-20102-retire-saved-report-stack`
Reviewed-by: `session_013RWUA7bNq5bRhehLPqXwMg`

**VERDICT: FAIL**

## Blocking findings to fix

1. **`os validate` / `os build` still give the misleading typo advice for `reports`** (finding ①4). Make `renderCapabilityMessage`'s `unknown` case in `packages/cli/src/utils/capability-preflight.ts:96` (or `classifyRequiredCapability` at `platform-capabilities.ts:422`) consult `RETIRED_PLATFORM_CAPABILITY_GUIDANCE` and emit the prescription, and pin it (a unit case on `renderCapabilityMessage`, or a plain-object-config e2e beside `build-json-advisory-parity.e2e.test.ts`). Whether that door refuses or warns follows the existing warn-first posture, but the text must be the retirement prescription, not "check for a typo".
2. **The published skill still enumerates `reports` as a live token mapped to `@objectstack/plugin-reports`** — `skills/objectstack-platform/SKILL.md:369` (finding ①5). Drop `reports` from that row (Tier H, but the PR is already Tier H), or, if the maintainer prefers to carry it separately, list the hit in the PR body with its reason and file the follow-up so the acceptance grep ledger is complete.

Non-blocking, fix if convenient: the docblock citation at `platform-capabilities.ts:85` names the wrong test file; the present-tense "one of only two … `ReportsServicePlugin` is the other" comments at `packages/runtime/src/external-validation-plugin.ts:240` and `external-validation-shutdown-clears-timers.test.ts:19`; the unlisted `sys_saved_report.format` rationale string at `object-field-editor-panel-echo-decisions.test.ts:304`.
